subject: Discovery recap: data protection & logging constraints — scope + next actions
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@cardinaltech.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@cardinaltech.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — retention & redaction constraints

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Thanks for the call today — good overview and appreciate you walking through Redwood's serving model. I wanted to capture CardinalTech's key constraints so we're aligned before the technical deep-dive: 

Pain points / constraints we reiterated today:
- PII handling: customer payment and PII must not be stored in cleartext in long-term logs. We need per-request redaction for card numbers, email, SSNs before any persistent storage.
- Retention windows: raw model input/outputs cannot be retained longer than 30 days. Audit logs that record access events are allowed to be retained for up to 7 years for compliance, but they must not contain raw PII.
- KV cache: we need the option to disable persistent KV cache and ensure ephemeral caches do not write to durable storage.
- Audit schema: logs must include user_id (hashed), request_id, model_id, timestamp, latency, and policy tags (e.g., pii_flag, retention_tier).
- Encryption & key management: all at-rest encryption must support our KMS (AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs) and we need evidence of key rotation policy.
- Regulatory: must be able to sign a BAA (HIPAA) and provide SOC 2 Type II artifacts.

Success criteria from CardinalTech's side:
- S1: Demonstrable redaction pipeline that guarantees no raw PII in storage (automated tests / sample artifacts).
- S2: Ability to configure retention per data class (raw, redacted, audit) from the console or API.
- S3: Audit logs exported to our S3 with a documented schema and retention lifecycle.
- S4: Latency < 200ms  p95 for sessionized inference in production on committed capacity.

Requested deliverables / next steps from Redwood:
1) Architecture diagram showing where data is redacted and which components write audit logs (PDF).
2) Sample audit log schema (CSV or JSON lines).
3) Confirmation of KV cache behavior and an option to disable persistent caching.
4) SOC 2 summary & contact for compliance review; BAA template if possible.
5) Indicative timeline for a private deployment (VPC) and an initial sizing for dedicated capacity.

We're targeting a security review the week of 2026-05-25, so having the artifacts by 2026-05-20 would be ideal. Also copying Michael (security lead) for procurement questions.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Sr. Security Program Manager
CardinalTech

Attachments: cardinal_security_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with initial questionnaire)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@cardinaltech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — retention & redaction constraints

Alice — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming receipt and restating commitments so there's no ambiguity on scope.

We captured the same constraints on our end. Short responses inline: 
- Redaction: We can plug a configurable redaction filter at the ingress point (pre-model) that removes/replaces card numbers, emails, SSNs by default. We will also provide test vectors showing the transformation.
- Retention: Redwood supports per-class retention policies via the Console and API. We will propose a default mapping (raw inputs: 30d, redacted transcripts: 365d, audit events: 7y) but these are configurable.
- KV cache: Option to run with ephemeral-only KV caching (in-memory only) — we will document the modes and default to disabled for your account until you enable it.
- Audit schema & export: we will provide a JSON-lines sample schema and a connector to export to your S3 in compressed, encrypted files.
- KMS & BAA / SOC2: We support AWS KMS CMKs and can share SOC 2 summary and contact. We'll surface BAA templates used in prior HIPAA engagements.

Proposed next steps (we can adjust):
- Tech deep-dive (90m) w/ Redwood infra + compliance lead: 2026-05-13 or 2026-05-14 — please indicate preferred slot.
- Deliver artifacts (arch diagram, audit schema, KV behavior doc, SOC2 summary, BAA template) by 2026-05-18.
- Pricing sketch & capacity sizing (for dedicated pool) delivered 2026-05-18.

I'll attach a high-level data flow diagram and start drafting the audit schema now. Karthik — can you be the eng owner for the deep-dive?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@cardinaltech.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-10T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — retention & redaction constraints

Lauren / Karthik,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Two clarifications from procurement/security: 
1) The audit log schema needs to include an immutable action_id and a reference to the stored artifact location (if present) — we cannot accept logs that point to unversioned storage blobs without references.
2) For the SOC2 artifacts, we only need the system description and the control matrix initially — we can request more during the security review.

Also — please include an indicative monthly cost range for a committed dedicated pool sized for ~100 requests/s steady-state and a burst to 300 rps. We don't need an exact MSRP yet, just a ballpark to route internally.

One more ask: can you include a sample redaction test (before/after) for three records (card number, customer email, SSN) so our security team can see deterministic behavior?

Thanks — we are available for the 2026-05-14 slot for the deep-dive.

Michael Torres
Director, Procurement
CardinalTech
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@cardinaltech.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@cardinaltech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — retention & redaction constraints

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications. Quick summary of agreed action items & owners: 

Action items:
- Redwood to deliver artifacts (Owner: lauren_bishop) by 2026-05-18: architecture diagram (PDF), audit schema (JSONL sample), redaction test vectors (3 samples), KV cache behavior doc
- Redwood eng (Owner: karthik_iyer) to run the 90m technical deep-dive on 2026-05-14 at 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite to follow)
- Redwood pricing & sizing (Owner: lauren_bishop) — ballpark for 100 rps steady / 300 rps burst by 2026-05-18
- CardinalTech to run internal security review week of 2026-05-25 and provide feedback / list of required artifacts (Owner: Alice Nguyen)
